closes: Adds Mondrian (category-conditional) conformal prediction to the module UQ battery.
Demonstrates and quantifies conditional under-coverage of ordinary marginal conformal across Tg and molecular-weight subgroups on OpenPoly Tg.
Closes the group-conditional-coverage item left open by jackknife-plus-cvplus-openpoly-tg-v1.
does_not_close: Does not establish wet-lab qualification, batch release, or human parity.

Category-conditional coverage is guaranteed only up to finite-sample slack (~n_cal per category); exact-conditional (per-point) coverage is impossible distribution-free (Vovk 2012, Lei-Wasserman 2014).
Ridge base learner is a deterministic reference, not the module's production predictor.
Taxonomy is a fixed tercile partition; adaptive/normalized-nonconformity Mondrian (Bostrom 2021) remains untested.

G3_label_permutation_control.note: Under permuted calibration residuals there is no real per-category signal; recorded observationally.

headline: Mondrian (category-conditional) conformal prediction (Vovk-Lindsay-Nouretdinov-Gammerman 2003; Vovk-Gammerman-Shafer 2005) is added to the tolerance-robustness UQ battery, closing the group-conditional-coverage gap left open by the signed jackknife+/CV+ receipt. On OpenPoly experimental Tg (n=442) with the SAME fixed Ridge base learner, seed and 50/50 calibration split as the signed split-conformal method, ordinary marginal conformal holds 0.938 marginal coverage yet its WORST tercile falls to 0.857 (predicted-Tg taxonomy) / 0.925 (log10-MW taxonomy); Mondrian per-category calibration lifts the worst tercile to 0.946 / 0.952 respectively at the cost of heteroscedastic category-specific widths. Two-replay byte-stable; 4/4 known-answer gates pass.

log10_MW_terciles.taxonomy_source: explicit input feature log10(molecular_weight); never uses label

predicted_Tg_terciles.taxonomy_source: frozen proper-train Ridge prediction (function of x only)

non_circularity: Ordinary split-conformal and Mondrian split-conformal share ONE fixed base learner, seed, 60/40 pool/test split, 50/50 proper-train/calibration partition and test set. The ONLY difference is global vs per-category conformity quantile, so every coverage/width difference is attributable to the Mondrian taxonomy. Both taxonomies are computable from x alone without the test label (predicted-Tg via the frozen proper-train model; log10-MW is an explicit input feature). Target labels are experimental Tg from OpenPoly.
purpose: Add Mondrian (category-conditional) conformal prediction to the tolerance-robustness UQ battery and test whether per-category calibration restores >= (1-alpha) coverage inside subgroups where ordinary marginal conformal under-covers -- the relevant robustness property when a formulation lands in a specific Tg or molecular-weight regime.
theory_reference: Vovk, Lindsay, Nouretdinov, Gammerman 2003, Mondrian Confidence Machine, Tech. Report, Royal Holloway Univ. London
Vovk, Gammerman, Shafer 2005, Algorithmic Learning in a Random World, Springer, Ch. 4.5 (Mondrian conformal predictors), ISBN 978-0-387-00152-4
Papadopoulos, Proedrou, Vovk, Gammerman 2002, Inductive Confidence Machines for Regression (ICML) - ordinary split-conformal baseline
Hoerl, Kennard 1970, Ridge Regression (Technometrics) - base learner
Clopper, Pearson 1934, The use of confidence or fiducial limits, Biometrika 26(4):404-413 - exact per-category coverage CI
